governanceNotes: Deferral reason 1 (variant-versus-disease identity): the reference literature itself defines clinodactyly under 10 degrees as a normal physiologic variant, and pathologic cases are described anatomically (trapezoidal/triangular phalangeal shape causing coronal-plane deviation) rather than as a progressive acquired condition; there is no acquired secondary condition in the catalog that clinodactyly could cause or aggravate, and authoring an edge to trigger-finger or contracture identities would invent a mechanical relationship the literature does not document.

Deferral reason 2 (syndrome-confounded literature): the clinodactyly literature is dominated by genetic-syndrome associations (dozens of GeneReviews entries list it as a feature), which document co-occurrence with syndromic diagnoses rather than outcomes; drafting an edge on that base would map a congenital-anomaly marker as if it were a disease pathway, violating the CRG's etiological-integrity requirement.

Surgical-technique context recorded: the osteotomy literature treats severe clinodactyly as a static deformity corrected for cosmesis or function, with no documented progression to other catalogued conditions; recorded as context, not as comorbidity evidence.
